name: FRANCE, Ali

headline.note: Some full-time UK communications work is supported, but its boundaries are unknown. A dated March 2004 NHS archive identifies France under her former name as a Commission for Health Improvement press contact immediately before that body's replacement by the Healthcare Commission. This resolves a predecessor employer observation, not a 2002 start or continuous payroll transfer. Journalism, later private work, care/medical leave and self-employment lack sufficient hours or endpoints for totals. Excluded political, nonprofit, care, sport and elected roles remain separate. Missing evidence is not zero.

career_spells.role: Bachelor of Arts student (journalism and politics)
career_spells.evidence_note: France explicitly identifies degree completion1996 and USQ in government press-conference transcript. Prior1997 inference from later work start removed. Start and study load remain unknown.
career_spells.counting_note: Study is excluded from the employment headlines.

career_spells.evidence_note: Her first speech confirms the employer and sequence. ABC reports that she worked there for three years until 2000; the profile aggregation gives 1998-2000. Exact appointment, cessation, hours and leave are unavailable. Father’s April2001 speech independently identifies Courier-Mail work in Brisbane and Townsville; does not establish separate employer or regional posting dates.
career_spells.counting_note: Private employment is supported, but substantive full-time status and exact boundaries are not sufficiently evidenced for a duration.

career_spells.employer: Hong Kong Standard / Hong Kong iMail
career_spells.evidence_note: France's first speech confirms Hong Kong court reporting after The Courier-Mail, and a 2025 profile identifies the Hong Kong Standard. Month boundaries appear only in a secondary professional-profile aggregation; hours and leave are not established. April2001 speech supplies contemporaneous employment snapshot in Hong Kong; leave taken to assist father’s election campaign is mentioned but pay basis unknown.
career_spells.counting_note: Employer and role are supported, but the evidence is insufficient for a full-time private duration.

career_spells.evidence_note: A 2025 profile says France worked for Westminster Council, while the profile aggregation supplies a one-month listing. The exact legal interval, hours and relationship to the Healthcare Commission start remain unresolved. The January2002 same-month interval is not independently confirmed; removed2002 Healthcare Commission start must not be used to resolve it.
career_spells.counting_note: Public employer is supported, but employment duration and full-time status are not.

career_spells.role: Senior Press Officer; communications work on state-of-healthcare reports
career_spells.evidence_note: First speech supports communications work on first two healthcare reports and full-time work before2006 care break. Aggregator2002-01 start withdrawn: body legally established2004 and operationalApril2004. Possible predecessor employment is a lead, not established fact. Actual start and predecessor/Westminster transition unknown.2006 end kept at year precision from first-person account; January endpoint unconfirmed. Regulator is an executive NDPB with ministerial appointments, coded public service, not a trading public corporation. Whole-period hours and leave unknown.
career_spells.counting_note: Public control and some full-time work are supported, but the full-time boundaries are insufficient for a duration calculation.

career_spells.evidence_note: France says she left full-time employment after her younger son was born and returned to a part-time job after four years. The year boundaries are approximate; they are retained as reported rather than converted to exact dates.
career_spells.counting_note: Unpaid care is recorded separately and excluded from the public/private employment headlines.

career_spells.employer: Carbon Media Pty Ltd / Carbon Creative
career_spells.role: Communications worker; television producer and script writer
career_spells.evidence_note: France says Wayne Denning first hired her part-time after a four-year care break and gave her an ABC documentary within a year. Screen Australia credits her as producer and writer of Carbon Media's 2010 documentary proppaNOW. The profile aggregation lists January 2009-January 2011, which does not align perfectly with the approximate four-year account; year precision is retained and the discrepancy flagged.
career_spells.counting_note: The job was expressly part-time and no defensible FTE fraction is available, so it is excluded from the full-time headline.

career_spells.evidence_note: France reports six surgeries in four years after the 2011 accident and being told she was unlikely to work again. This represents a documented employment interruption, not an assertion that no paid work occurred throughout the entire year range.
career_spells.counting_note: Medical recovery is not employment and is excluded.

career_spells.evidence_note: Public biographies identify France as a world champion para-athlete and record international competition in 2016. No evidence establishes that this was paid employment.
career_spells.counting_note: Sporting activity without evidence of employment is excluded.

career_spells.evidence_note: A public professional-profile aggregation lists motivational speaking from January 2017. Trading identity, workload, continuity, leave and cessation after election to Parliament are not established.
career_spells.counting_note: Self-employment may be private-sector work, but substantive full-time duration is unsupported.

career_spells.evidence_note: The employer, title and month boundaries appear in a public professional-profile aggregation. Employer records, hours, leave and overlap with self-employment have not been located. Publicly indexed 16 March 2018 contemporaneous report independently identifies communications work with Karuna. It does not confirm managerial title, hours or actual cessation; month boundaries remain aggregation-only.
career_spells.counting_note: Nonprofit employment is excluded under the current headline method.

career_spells.employer: Office of the Hon. Steven Miles MP
career_spells.role: Political staff member, role not identified
career_spells.evidence_note: France calls Miles a former boss, and ABC and contemporary reporting identify her as a former staffer in his office. The job title, employing entity, dates, hours, leave and overlaps are not published.
career_spells.counting_note: Political staff employment is excluded irrespective of public funding.

career_spells.role: Federal candidate for Dickson in 2019, 2022 and 2025
career_spells.evidence_note: France describes seven years campaigning for Dickson and contested three elections. This span records political activity with campaign breaks; it is not evidence of continuous paid employment. Pay, leave and overlaps with other roles and 18 months caring for her son are unresolved. Earlier2May end was an election-eve proxy; exact cessation of campaign activity is not independently established.
career_spells.counting_note: Candidate and party activity is excluded from the two employment headlines.

career_spells.evidence_note: Official parliamentary service starts with the 3 May 2025 election.
career_spells.counting_note: Federal elected office is excluded from the employment headlines.

career_spells.role: Press contact; exact job title unconfirmed
career_spells.evidence_note: An archived official CHI news release dated 10 March 2004 names Ali Lawlor as the further-information contact. The former-name identity is supported by contemporaneous reporting after her 2011 accident and by her father's 2001 speech and Hong Kong byline. The release states CHI would cease on 31 March and be replaced by the Commission for Healthcare Audit and Inspection on 1 April. This is a dated employment observation only: it does not prove commencement, hours, service through 31 March or automatic transfer to the successor.
career_spells.counting_note: Public-sector communications work is directly observed, but no calculable interval or substantive full-time status is established.

career_spells.evidence_note: First speech states she joined Labor in2016 and began involvement through Labor Enabled before a state-seat preselection. This is party participation, not proof of a paid appointment; exact activity boundaries and remuneration unknown.
career_spells.counting_note: Party activity is excluded; membership year is not an employment start.

research_notes: Official parliamentary occupation data contains no pre-parliament occupation entries; the timeline therefore relies heavily on France's first speech, employer credit and public reporting.

The public profile aggregation is used as a lead for month dates, not as conclusive payroll evidence. The Carbon start date conflicts slightly with the approximate four-year care break in France's speech.

Follow up News Corp and Hong Kong employment records, Westminster/Healthcare Commission transition and hours, Carbon Media appointment/cessation, Karuna hours, Ali France Creative workload, and the title/dates of the Steven Miles role.
Resolve work, leave and campaign boundaries during accident recovery, the 2019/2022 campaigns, and the 18-month care period ending in February 2024.

2026-10-02 follow-up: degree year corrected to1996 from government transcript; healthcare-regulator identity/date conflict documented using UK public-body records; added contemporary2001 Hong Kong/Courier-Mail location corroboration. Searched France and Lawlor names for commission/Westminster, internship and Karuna employer evidence: no primary individual appointment or hours found. ANU Australian National Internships Program appears in aggregator education; retain as follow-up lead pending primary confirmation, dates and placement host. Do not assign UK rehabilitation-officer namesake or other speakers’ career details. Priority next: primary profile, predecessor regulator2002–04, first two report acknowledgements and Karuna2017–18 personnel/annual reports; no contact details used.

2026-10-03 follow-up: NHS England's Gosport archive yielded an original CHI news release naming Ali Lawlor as media contact on10March2004. Former-name identity is corroborated by her father's2001 speech/Hong Kong byline and contemporaneous2011 accident reporting. This establishes work at the Healthcare Commission predecessor shortly before the statutory1April transition, but not a2002 start, weekly hours, uninterrupted employment or automatic payroll transfer. The predecessor is therefore a separate dated observation. Searches for additional CHI/CHAI releases, first two state-of-healthcare report credits, Westminster appointment and Karuna personnel records did not yet resolve intervals. Next: archived press-office directories/reports, Westminster personnel material, Karuna annual reports and Steven Miles office appointment.

2026-10-04 follow-up: exact-name searches for Ali Lawlor with the Healthcare Commission/CHI, Karuna personnel material and Steven Miles office records produced no new original appointment, payroll, hours or endpoint evidence. Results repeated the public profile aggregation and media description of a busy communications career. The March 2004 CHI release remains the only dated primary UK personnel observation; no uninterrupted transfer to the successor body is inferred. Next decisive evidence: archived regulator press-office directory/report acknowledgements, Westminster or Karuna personnel record, or a Miles-office appointment notice.

Targeted follow-up2026-10-05: Added previously omitted Labor Enabled party participation from primary first speech; paid appointment and dates remain unknown. Regulator2005 and Karuna annual-report searches yielded no new individual personnel record. No2002 Healthcare Commission commencement or automatic predecessor transfer inferred. Priority remains original press-office/report credits or Westminster/Karuna personnel material.

Targeted second follow-up 2026-10-05: independent contemporaneous March 2018 indexed report corroborates Karuna communications role; no unseen full-page facts or exact endpoint adopted. Public Karuna-site searches did not locate personnel record. Former-name regulator searches led back to the existing Gosport CHI release; contributor page exposes no further substantive document text. 2011 employer-comment news lead returns403; not used beyond recorded lead.
